title: Something new
text: With more free time, you're thinking about a new hobby.

outcomes.text: My tomatoes are the envy of the street.
A squirrel cleaned out the tomatoes overnight. I bought a cage and declared war.
I grew roses that took a prize at the county fair. I've never been so proud.
I painted a portrait of my family. Everyone looks a bit like a potato.
A neighbour bought one of my paintings for ten dollars. It is the first money I've ever earned from art.
My hands shake more than I expected. The paintings look abstract now, and people call that a style.
Our team is called the Gutter Gang. We're terrible and happy.
I tore a muscle in week two. I bowled the rest of the season sitting down.
We won the league in our final game, and the trophy sits on my mantel.
I started writing down my life story.
Halfway through I realised how much I'd forgotten. I phoned an old friend to fill in the gaps, and it became a weekly call.
I finished the book and printed ten copies. Each of my children received one. One of them cried.

title: Urgent call
text: A caller claims your grandchild is in jail and needs $3,000 wired right now.

outcomes.text: It was a scam. The money is gone.
The bank called me an hour later and got most of it back. I trembled for the rest of the day.
They called back the next day for more. I sent it, too. My family found out after.
I hung up. Nice try.
I phoned my grandchild to check. They were perfectly fine and thought the story hilarious.
I hung up but my hands shook for an hour. The call had sounded so real.

choices.label: Keep them talking for an hour

outcomes.text: I told them about my knee surgery in great detail. They hung up on me.
They called again the next day. By the third call I'd named them all.
I accidentally gave them my date of birth. My bank was not amused.
I found my old high school yearbook and laughed at my haircut.
I found an old love letter in a shoebox and read it twice.
Just a bruise. The doctor said to be careful.
I broke my hip. Recovery was long.
I walked it off. Mostly.
Walking it off wasn't enough. A week later I was in the emergency room with a cracked rib.
I was fine, but my daughter insisted on installing handrails. I complained and then used them daily.
My daughter was there in twenty minutes. She cried, then fussed, then got a doctor.
I called, and nobody answered. I found myself alone on the stairs with time to think.
{kid.first} came to visit and cooked me dinner.
{kid.first} called just to say {kid.he} loves me.
